acceptOwnership().details: The new owner accepts the ownership transfer.

acquire(address,uint256,address,address,.details: Returns 0 because settlement is asynchronous. The        IndexToken records expected/attested amounts via        `IAsyncAssetAdapter.previewAsync` and the IntentQueue.

params.hints: ABI-encoded `(uint256 minOutNativeUnits)` — passed        through to THORChain's `LIM` field on the swap memo.

returns.reported: Output delivered this tx (0 allowed only for async).

assetForm(address).details: Used by `IndexToken` to branch into sync vs async settlement paths.      MUST be consistent across calls for the same `targetToken`.

cancelAcquire(bytes32,uint256,address,ui.details: Pure event emission. The funding token already left to        THORChain at `acquire` time and is not recoverable from        this adapter; the cancel event is the off-chain executor's        signal to attempt a swap-back / mark the deposit orphan.        Cancel id is derived deterministically from        `(chainId, self, intentId, slotIndex)` so the same        cancellation always produces the same id.

params.amount: The funding amount that was originally dispatched        for this slot. Carried for the off-chain executor's        accounting; the adapter does not act on it on-chain.
params.hints: Adapter-specific routing data; may be empty.
params.intentId: The IntentQueue id whose mint was cancelled.
params.slotIndex: The intent-local slot index this adapter handled.

returns.cancelId: Deterministic identifier emitted on the cancel         event for off-chain deduplication.

params.factory_: {IIndexFactory} whose registered IndexToken clones are        the only authorized callers of the dispatch entry-points.
params.initialOwner: Owner permitted to rotate the native custody address.
params.memoAsset_: THORChain asset string for the swap memo (e.g. "BTC.BTC").
params.targetTokenSentinel: Stable address used in IndexToken        baskets to refer to this asset (factory allowlists this).
params.vaultRegistry_: The {ThorchainVaultRegistry} that mirrors the current Asgard vault.

owner().details: Returns the address of the current owner.

pendingOwner().details: Returns the address of the pending owner.

previewAsync(address,uint256,bytes).details: Pre-trade quoting against THORChain pool depth would        require an external oracle call. v1 returns 0 for        `expectedAmount` and lets the off-chain side fill in the        attested amount — IndexToken mints based on attested, not        expected, so an inaccurate preview does not affect share        accounting.

params.amountIn: Amount of the funding token allocated to this slot.
params.targetToken: Canonical asset identifier address (or sentinel        the adapter understands; see adapter docs).

returns.assetId: The canonical asset identifier (e.g.         `keccak256("BTC.BTC")`) the AttestationOracle will attest         against.
returns.expectedAmount: Adapter's quote in the native asset's         smallest units.

recoverStuckToken(address,address).details: Last-resort path for funds stuck if e.g. the Router fails to        pull an approved deposit (broken-router scenario). Owner-only;        `forceApprove(0)` at the end of `acquire` already prevents        post-tx pulls, so this only applies to genuinely orphaned        tokens. Reverts if the contract has zero balance to make        accidental misuse loud.

redeemAsync(address,uint256,bytes,bytes).details: Emits `RedeemDispatched` for the off-chain executor.        The intent id binds a per-adapter monotonic nonce so two        same-block redemptions from the same originator with        identical (amount, recipient) produce DISTINCT ids — the        executor can safely deduplicate by id without dropping a        legitimate second redemption.

params.amount: Pro-rata amount the user is owed (in the native        asset's smallest units, as tracked by the off-chain        custody — for v1 this is the amount the Bitcoin multisig        will send to `nativeRecipient`).
params.nativeRecipient: Raw bytes of the user's native-chain        address (e.g. encoded BTC bech32 string).

returns.intentId: Off-chain intent identifier the executor uses         to deduplicate.

renounceOwnership().details: Leaves the contract without owner. It will not be possible to call `onlyOwner` functions. Can only be called by the current owner. NOTE: Renouncing ownership will leave the contract without an owner, thereby disabling any functionality that is only available to the owner.

setNativeCustodyAddress(string).details: Affects all future deposits. In-flight intents already        directed at the previous address must settle to the        previous address — by design, off-chain ops should pause        new mints during rotation, drain or reconcile in-flight        intents, then update.

transferOwnership(address).details: Starts the ownership transfer of the contract to a new account. Replaces the pending transfer if there is one. Can only be called by the current owner. Setting `newOwner` to the zero address is allowed; this can be used to cancel an initiated ownership transfer.

ASSET_ID().notice: Canonical asset identifier the AttestationOracle attests         against. Computed off-chain as `keccak256(memoAsset)`.

DEFAULT_EXPIRY_OFFSET().notice: Default deposit expiry offset above `block.timestamp`,         in seconds. THORChain requires ≥ 3600. Defaulted to 7200         to give the Router transaction comfortable headroom.

FACTORY().notice: IndexFactory whose registered IndexToken clones are the only         authorized callers of `acquire` / `redeemAsync` / `cancelAcquire`.

MAX_VAULT_AGE().notice: Maximum age (seconds) of the registry's vault cache that         `acquire` will accept. THORChain Asgard rotates per churn         (~3 days) with retired vaults active for ~6 hours;         12 hours is a comfortable bot-SLA + grace margin.

TARGET_TOKEN_SENTINEL().notice: Sentinel address used by IndexToken baskets to refer to         this adapter's native asset (e.g. a stable, non-colliding         address derived from the asset name).

VAULT_REGISTRY().notice: On-chain mirror of the current Asgard vault address.

assetForm(address).notice: Declares how `targetToken` is delivered by this adapter.

cancelAcquire(bytes32,uint256,address,ui.notice: Notifies the adapter that an in-flight async acquire was         cancelled by IndexToken (deadline elapsed without a full         attestation). The funding token has already been         dispatched to the partner network at `acquire` time and is         therefore unrecoverable from this adapter's surface; this         method exists purely as the on-chain signal an off-chain         executor watches to attempt a swap-back / orphan         reconciliation.

previewAsync(address,uint256,bytes).notice: Adapter's pre-trade estimate of the amount that will be         delivered on the native chain after THORChain's swap +         outbound fees.

recoverStuckToken(address,address).notice: Recover ERC20 tokens accidentally left in this adapter.

redeemAsync(address,uint256,bytes,bytes).notice: Dispatches a native-chain withdrawal back to a         user-controlled address. Called by IndexToken during burn         for native slots.

setNativeCustodyAddress(string).notice: Rotates the native-chain destination address. Owner-only.

      so two same-block burns by the same originator with identical

@title ThorchainAdapter
 @notice `IAssetAdapter` implementation that routes a single native
         asset through the THORChain Ethereum Router. One adapter
         instance handles one (asset, native-custody-address) pair —
         deploy a separate instance per asset (BTC, BNB, AVAX, …).
 @dev   Mint flow:
          1. IndexToken `safeTransfer`s `amountIn` of `fundingToken` here.
          2. IndexToken calls `acquire(...)`. We resolve the current
             Asgard vault (caller-supplied hint, falling back to the
             registry), build a `=:ASSET:DESTADDR:MIN` swap memo, set
             a fresh allowance to the Router, and call
             `depositWithExpiry`. Returns `0` because settlement is
             asynchronous.
          3. Off-chain attestation signers observe the BTC arrival at
             our `nativeCustodyAddress`, post k-of-n EIP-712 sigs to
             AttestationOracle, which forwards to IntentQueue.
          4. Once the IntentQueue intent is fully attested, IndexToken
             reads the attested amount and mints shares.
        Burn flow:
          1. IndexToken calls `redeemAsync` with the user's
             native-chain address as `nativeRecipient`.
          2. We emit `RedeemDispatched` for the off-chain executor,
             which constructs and broadcasts a Bitcoin multisig
             transaction sending the user's pro-rata BTC.
        Security model:
          - Only `Ownable2Step` admin can rotate the native-custody
            address (changes destination of all future deposits).
          - The Router is `immutable`. Vault is fetched live (rotates).
          - Funding allowance to Router is set via `forceApprove(amount)`
            then back to 0 in the same call to handle USDT's
            non-standard `approve` behaviour and avoid lingering allowance.
          - `assetForm` returns NATIVE_OFF_CHAIN exclusively; this
            adapter cannot be used as a sync adapter even if the
            factory bypasses its registration check.
